title: Modernization of Dairy Sector and Growth in Milk Production
subtitle: NPDD and AHIDF Accelerate Modernisation and Capacity Building in Dairy Sector
body_text:
The Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, stated that the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, is implementing various schemes and programmes to complement and supplement the efforts of State Governments in strengthening, modernising and promoting the dairy sector. These initiatives are aimed at enhancing milk production and productivity, improving dairy infrastructure and value-chain development, strengthening milk processing and marketing facilities, and improving the overall efficiency and sustainability of the dairy sector.
National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD): Under NPDD, 50% grant assistance is provided for strengthening milk procurement, chilling, and quality assurance infrastructure to increase the share of organized milk procurement in the country. Further, 75% Central Grant assistance is provided for establishing modern milk procurement, dairy processing, value addition, and cold chain infrastructure, and 70% Central Grant assistance is extended for setting up quality assurance infrastructure, only in hilly areas and the North Eastern Region (NER). Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF): Under AHIDF 3% interest subvention is provided to eligible beneficiaries to establish modern dairy processing, value addition, and cold chain infrastructure projects in both the cooperative and private sectors.
As of June 2026, 36,611 new Dairy Cooperative Societies (DCS) have been organised and 34,557 DCS strengthened at the village level with financial assistance under National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD), Further, about 168 lakh litres per day (LLPD) of milk chilling capacity has been created, and 76,748 quality testing devices distributed. Under Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF), projects with a total milk processing and value‑addition capacity of 418 LLPD have been approved in both cooperative and private sectors.
The year-wise details of milk production and per capita milk availability in the country from 2020-21 to 2024-25 is as under:
Year Milk Production (Million Metric Tonnes)/Year Per Capita Availability (Gram /day) 2020-21 209.96 427.00 2021-22 222.07 446.00 2022-23 230.58 459.00 2023-24 239.30 471.00 2024-25 247.87 485.00
The ongoing schemes aim to strengthen and modernize the infrastructure for milk collection, cold storage, processing, and value addition in the dairy sector. These efforts provide an organized market for milk producers and help improve their income.
***

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying informed Parliament about progress under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) and the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF), which support modernization of dairy infrastructure across India. As of June 2026, over 71,000 Dairy Cooperative Societies have been organised or strengthened, 168 LLPD of milk chilling capacity created, and AHIDF-approved projects add 418 LLPD of processing capacity. Milk production rose from 209.96 million metric tonnes in 2020-21 to 247.87 million metric tonnes in 2024-25, with per capita availability increasing from 427 to 485 grams/day.
enrichment.context:
India is the world's largest milk producer, and dairying is a critical livelihood source for millions of rural households, particularly landless and marginal farmers, with women playing a significant role in dairy cooperatives. The NPDD (restructured version of earlier dairy development programmes) and AHIDF (launched in 2020 to promote private investment in dairy, meat and animal feed infrastructure) are key Central Sector schemes under the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) aimed at building an organized dairy value chain—from village-level cooperative societies to milk chilling, processing, and quality testing infrastructure—thereby reducing wastage, ensuring better price realization for farmers, and expanding formal market access. AHIDF specifically incentivizes private and cooperative investment through interest subvention, addressing gaps in cold chain and processing capacity that limit value addition.

These schemes complement the broader 'White Revolution' legacy associated with Operation Flood and Amul-style cooperative dairying, and align with government priorities of doubling farmers' income, promoting food processing (Ministry of Food Processing Industries synergy), and strengthening rural non-farm employment. Special provisions for hilly and North Eastern states (higher central grant share) reflect the government's focus on balanced regional development and integrating remote areas into national value chains. Steady growth in milk production and per capita availability also has implications for nutritional security, given milk's role as an affordable protein source in Indian diets.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)' primarily aims to provide which of the following incentives to eligible beneficiaries?
options: Direct cash subsidy for purchasing dairy cattle
3% interest subvention for setting up dairy processing and cold chain infrastructure
Free veterinary services for organized dairy farmers
100% tax exemption on milk sales revenue
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, AHIDF provides 3% interest subvention to eligible beneficiaries in both cooperative and private sectors for establishing modern dairy processing, value addition, and cold chain infrastructure projects.

prelims_questions.question: As per the data cited in a recent government release, what was India's per capita milk availability (grams/day) in 2024-25?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states per capita milk availability rose to 485 grams/day in 2024-25, up from 427 grams/day in 2020-21.
